title: 1-05 Kraken Bay
body:
### Background and Hook(s) - This is likely the fourth area explored by the players, and is tailored toward the level bands of 9 - 13 and 11 - 15, meaning creatures with CR maxing out at about 16. - There is a Kraken here, but should be treated as a late-stage boss that's telegraphed as deadly and returned to at a later point. ### Characters and Locations - #### ★11: The Luminous Drift (Irian MZ) - [x] ✅ 2026-03-30 > The water here is not dark. It is not lit from above or below—it simply _glows_, every cubic foot of it alive with drifting motes of luminescent plankton that pulse in slow, arrhythmic waves. Suspended among them, tumbling lazily in the current, are pale shards of something crystalline — dragonshards, buoyant with stored radiant energy, shedding warmth and light in equal measure. There are no shadows here. There is no depth. Distance becomes a guess. Something large and luminous moves through the haze ahead, and it is difficult to say how far away it is. - The plankton bloom exists because of the shards—Siberys radiation leaches into the water and feeds an explosion of bioluminescent microorganisms that have spread across the entire zone. The shards themselves float because Irian's positive energy and the sheer volume of plankton renders them buoyant; they drift in loose clusters, occasionally shedding smaller fragments that sink slowly before the current catches them again. - The light is not hostile, but it is relentless. Creatures in this zone cannot benefit from darkness or invisibility, and have disadvantage on Perception checks that rely on sight beyond 30 feet—not because visibility is low, but because contrast is nonexistent. Everything glows equally. - A shallow seabed shelf sits at the bottom of the zone, crusted with a denser concentration of grounded shards too heavy to float. This shelf is navigable but not the primary feature; most of the zone exists in open water. - The plankton bloom pulses downward in slow tidal cycles, and the sahuagin of Hal'iri below time their spawning rituals to coincide with the densest surges. The light visible from the city is not ambient—it is anticipated, tracked, and considered sacred by the Ta'har priests. - The **Incandescent One** drifts at the center of the densest shard cluster, drawn to the largest concentration of radiant energy. It is not territorial in the conventional sense—it simply treats the zone as its body and anything that disturbs the shards as an irritant. - Roll on the [[C06 The City Between#Random Discovery|Random Discovery]] table to determine what else is found here. > [!danger]- **Radiant Surge (Environmental Lair Action)** > On initiative count 20, a nearby shard pulses outward with stored energy. Each creature within 15 feet of any floating shard must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or be **blinded until the end of their next turn** as the light overwhelms their vision. Creatures with resistance or immunity to radiant damage automatically succeed. `encounter: 1: Incandescent One` #### ★11: Hal'iri - [ ] >Warm, golden light suffuses the water, refracting through living coral grown into graceful arcs. Bioluminescent flora pulse softly, responding to movement like a slow heartbeat. The water feels buoyant here, lighter than elsewhere, and the scent is clean and mineral-fresh. For a moment, the deep feels almost kind. - This is a stronghold of the Ta’har, driving mystical research and holding the largest temples in the Dominion—both in reality and in the kar’lassa’s dream. Many priests train in Hal’iri, and its people have grand dreams of what the Dominion can become. It’s a center for exploring lofty goals, such as defeating the Valraean Protectorate, consuming the overlords to gain their power, and perhaps even conquering the planes. - **Arcane Duels**. Formal arcane duels and demonstrations are common here, showcasing precision control and magical prowess rather than raw power. - **The Illumination Rites.** Periodic public ceremonies where promising spawn are exposed to shard light in open water during bloom cycles. Those that emerge changed are celebrated. Those that emerge wrong are fed to the kar'lassa. Players may witness a rite mid-session, be invited to observe as neutral parties, or arrive to find one gone badly wrong. ##### Locations - **Luminous Spire**. Where radiant magic is studied and weaponized under the guise of enlightenment. - **The Tide Altar.** An open-air temple platform positioned directly above the Sunken Eye below. During bloom cycles, the rising plankton light illuminates the altar from beneath, which the Ta'har interpret as divine confirmation. Irixa conducts her most controversial experiments here—exposing spawn to concentrated shard fragments smuggled up from below. The results are not always luminous sahuagin. Sometimes they are something else, and those are quietly disposed of before the priesthood notices. - **The Shard Vault.** A locked chamber where recovered Siberys fragments are stored, catalogued, and rationed. Access is restricted to Ta'har priests and Irixa. The largest fragment inside was hauled up from the Sunken Eye at significant cost—a piece broken free by the mining operation below. It pulses with more energy than anything else in the city and is visibly destabilizing the spawn exposed to it. Irixa knows. She hasn't stopped the experiments. - **Spawning Pools**. Eggs are exposed to constant regenerative energy from the bloom cycles above and shard fragments below. Deformities self-correct. Weakness is erased. Luminous sahuagin are created here—the Dominion's idealized forms: radiant bioluminescence, rapid healing, heightened perception. ##### Characters - **Irixa** (LN female sahuagin biomancer). Believes the Dominion can be perfected without constant slaughter, a view tolerated only because her results are undeniable. She is aware the vault fragment is destabilizing and considers it a variable to be managed, not a reason to stop. - **Verath the Radiant** (LE male sahuagin Ta'har high priest). Tall, with skin that bioluminesces faintly even at rest—a result of decades of shard exposure he considers proof of divine favor. He genuinely believes the Dominion is destined to consume the planes and regards Irixa's pragmatism as heresy dressed in results. He knows the vault fragment is unstable and considers it an acceleration, not a problem. #### ★11: The Sunken Eye - [x] ✅ 2026-03-23 > The light here does not diffuse—it _columns_. A single colossal Siberys dragonshard, wider than a ship and driven vertically into the seabed like a thrown spear, emits a beam of pure radiant light straight upward through the water. Smaller shards orbit it in slow spirals, caught in its pull. The beam is visible from the surface. It is visible from Hal'iri above. It is visible from everywhere, and it has been visible for a very long time. Around its base, a framework of House Cannith scaffolding clings to the shard's lower face—drills, collection vessels, and tethered elemental subs. The operation is active. The workers have not noticed you yet. - The Sunken Eye is the source of the Luminous Drift above—Siberys radiation leaching upward feeds the plankton bloom, which the Ta'har of Hal'iri have built their theology around. They do not know a mining operation has been running at its base, breaking off fragments for extraction. The vault fragment in Hal'iri above is a direct product of this operation. - The radiant column functions as a passive scrying beacon. Anything passing through it is visible from the surface to anyone with the right equipment—which House Lyrandar has, aboard the survey vessels maintaining the operation from above. - The mining operation is a joint House Cannith and House Lyrandar venture. The workers are a mix of hired laborers, warforged, and bound elementals. They are not soldiers, but the operation has two dedicated security personnel who will respond to any interference. - A Prismatic Pearl is embedded in the face of the shard itself, visible at close range but unreachable without either navigating the mining operation or destroying part of the scaffolding—which will be noticed immediately. - **The Mining Operation**. The players have various options (or may make up their own) for retrieving the pearl: - **Negotiate.** The site supervisors have no particular loyalty to the shard or awareness of the pearl's significance. A compelling enough offer—or a sufficiently credible threat—may buy access. They will not hand over the pearl itself without authorization from House Cannith, but they can be convinced to look the other way. - **Sabotage.** Disabling the scaffolding, the elemental subs, or the extraction equipment forces an evacuation and clears the site. This takes time and creates noise, and risks damaging the shard itself—which will be felt in Hal'iri above as a bloom disruption, alerting Verath. - **Stealth.** The radiant column makes conventional stealth impossible within 30 feet of the shard. However, the orbiting smaller shards create brief, rotating blind spots in the column's intensity. A DC 15 Dexterity (Stealth) check made during a blind spot allows approach without triggering the scrying effect. Failure means the surface operation is alerted within the hour. `encounter: 1: Incandescent One` _(if not defeated in the Luminous Drift above)_ ##### Characters - **Overseer Dallen Mrak** (LN male human, House Cannith site supervisor). Efficient, document-obsessed, and deeply uncomfortable with anything that isn't in the operation's charter. He will not make decisions above his authority but can be stalled, bribed within his discretion, or bypassed entirely if the players make him someone else's problem. - **Tensyl** (N female warforged, House Lyrandar security lead). Stationed here because she is reliable and asks no questions about what the operation is actually disturbing. She has begun asking questions. She has not yet decided what to do with the answers. #### ✣2: Trolanport (Port) - [x] - Zilargo's capital is where almost anything can be commissioned, bought, or bound—elemental vessels, dragonshards, arcane components, and information. House Cannith, House Kundarak, and House Sivis all maintain major enclaves on the docks. The players can resupply and reequip here without difficulty. - The docks encourage vice deliberately. Every tavern, gambling den, and black market stall is a Trust operation or adjacent to one. Every conversation is being listened to by someone. - **The Trust Agent.** A gnome named **Pilli Soranno** approaches the players quietly, in a crowd, as if by accident. She knows about the Shard Vault in Hal'iri, the House Cannith mining survey that located the Sunken Eye, and—most usefully—that the Dominion hasn't retaliated against the mining operation yet, which means they're waiting for something. She will share all of this freely. Her request in return: the Pilgrim, alive and delivered to a location she will provide. - She will not explain why. The reason: the Trust intends to deliver the Pilgrim to the Valraean Protectorate as the true killer of the sea elf envoy. A small nation with no army survives by knowing things others don't—and delivering the murderer to the sea elves earns Zilargo enormous goodwill with a naval power that controls waters Trolanport depends on. Tidecrown twisting in diplomatic uncertainty in the meantime only increases the value of that gift. Pilli knows all of this. She will not say any of it. #### ✣3: Wyvernskull (Port) - [x] - Darguun's primary seaport does not hide what it is. The slave pens are on the docks. Prices are posted on boards outside them. Hobgoblin overseers move between cages without urgency, and no one on the waterfront pretends to be uncomfortable. This is commerce, conducted openly, and the city is proud of its efficiency. - This is the distinction from Tidecrown the players should feel without being told: Tidecrown's exploitation is hidden behind neutrality and polished diplomacy. Wyvernskull's is posted on a board by the harbor. The players should leave asking themselves which is actually worse. - Among the current inventory are a locathah and a kuo-toa, penned separately. - The **locathah**, Kenit, has seen the Pilgrim recently — within the last few weeks, moving through the Dark Sea with unusual purpose rather than the erratic behavior reported elsewhere. It was heading toward a specific ruin the locathah recognizes but can only describe in terms of currents and landmarks, not coordinates. - The **kuo-toa**, Prin, knows the Pilgrim by reputation among enslaved communities. It has become something like a folk figure — a kuo-toa that escaped, refused to be caught, and kept moving. The kuo-toa doesn't know what the Pilgrim is doing, but the stories it has heard suggest the Pilgrim is looking for something, not running from something. - Together, their information points toward a specific location in the Dark Sea. Neither can provide it alone. What the players do with this — buy their freedom, extract information and leave, or walk away entirely — is their problem. #### ✣4: Pylas Maradal (Port) - [x] ✅ 2026-05-18 - A Valenar port with a large House Lyrandar enclave and active shipyards. Its history as a smuggler's haven under Cyre's blind eye hasn't fully washed out — the docks are well-run on the surface and considerably less so underneath. - The shipyard is visibly busy. Players paying attention notice one vessel in dry dock being fitted with an extraction cradle unlike anything used for standard dragonshard recovery — purpose-built for something significantly larger. A DC 13 Investigation check or a conversation with any dockworker confirms it: the cradle is designed to lift and transport an object the size of a building. House Lyrandar is not planning to continue mining the Sunken Eye. They are planning to move it. - A DC 15 Persuasion or appropriate bribe gets a worker to confirm the commission came directly from a House Cannith artificer based in Sharn — not a field operation anymore, but a sanctioned extraction with significant institutional backing. #### ✣5: Newthrone (Port) - [x] ✅ 2026-05-18 - Q'barra's fortified capital sits at the edge of a continent that hasn't finished being explored. The docks are functional and rough, catering to prospectors, dragonshard hunters, and the occasional dragonborn delegation from the interior. Resupply is available but limited; the city prioritizes its own survival over visitor convenience. - **Zoril's Cartography** is impossible to miss. A hand-painted sign the width of the building face reads ZORIL — MAPS — ALL SEAS — ALL DEPTHS in six languages, two of which are wrong. The shopfront is plastered with oversized shell-plate samples, reference charts, and a running list of current prices chalked onto a board that gets updated every morning. Inside, shell-plate maps cover every surface—stacked in columns, hung from ceiling hooks, filed in open crates sorted by region, depth, and current direction. The organization appears chaotic and is in fact meticulous. Moving anything will be noticed immediately. - **Zoril** is the most accurate navigation resource available for the waters between Kraken Bay and the Dark Sea. He will sell charts for coin plus one piece of new information, however trivial—a depth reading, a current anomaly, a landmark description, anything he doesn't already have etched on a plate. Players who try to pay in information he already has get nothing and are told to come back with something better. - Returning to Zoril after exploring new areas of the campaign will consistently yield something useful in exchange for field observations. #### ♦3: Kraken Bay / Kraken Lair - [x] ✅ 2026-05-18 > The water changes before anything else does. Currents that ran steady and predictable begin to spiral inward, slow and patient, like water circling a drain too large to see. The color shifts—deep green giving way to black, not from depth but from something below absorbing the light. The seafloor, where visible, is scoured clean. No coral, no silt, no life. Just bare rock, gouged in parallel lines by something that dragged itself across it a very long time ago, and again not so long ago, and again recently. Ahead, the water is very still and very dark and very deep. Whatever made those marks is still here. - The players will not have a map marking this as a kraken's lair. They will know something is wrong before they know what it is. The environmental storytelling should do the work. - The spiral current is the first warning—ships that stop active navigation drift inward slowly but measurably. A DC 12 Perception check notices the drift; a DC 14 Nature check identifies it as something large enough to create its own gravitational pull in the water displacing the current. - The seafloor gouges are the second warning. Each parallel scar is roughly 8 feet wide and dozens of feet long. A DC 13 Nature or History check identifies them as tentacle drag marks. A DC 18 identifies the scale as kraken. - Debris rings the outer edge of the lair: shattered ship hulls, snapped masts, personal effects, and cargo drifting in slow orbits that never quite escape the current. Nothing is older than a few months. The kraken feeds regularly. - Any creature with a passive Perception of 14 or higher notices, at the edge of visibility, an enormous shape resting motionless in the dark below. It is not moving. It is aware. - Players who press further trigger the encounter. Players who turn back are allowed to leave without pursuit—this time. The kraken does not chase prey that retreats. It is patient in the way that things are patient when nothing has ever truly threatened them. `encounter: 1: Kraken` #### ⚔6: Adder Bay - [x] - With its proximity to Q'barra, Valenar, and the nearby manifest zone to Kythri, the small bay and the broader surrounding waters are home to dinosaurs, and a variety of chaotic creatures. | d10 | Encounter | | --: | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | 1 | **Murgrik Feeding Frenzy (CR ~11–12)**. Two double-mawed gators burst from a warm silt plume, snapping independently as they circle to keep the ship boxed in and prevent escape.
`encounter: 2: Murgrik` | | 2 | **Remorhaz Boilwake (CR 11)**. The bay boils as the creature tunnels beneath the seabed; it erupts in a scalding blast and attacks immediately, turning the area into rolling steam and churned silt.
`encounter: 1: Remorhaz` | | 3 | **Kelp Eel Tangle-Current (CR 10)**. A thick rope of living kelp, blades flensing as it coils, lashes up from a reef warped into impossible geometry by Kythri tides and strikes the first large thing that enters its territory.
`encounter: 1: Kelp Eel` | | 4 | **Illhveli, Kembingur — Blooded Leviathan (CR 12)**. A siege whale charges in a frenzy, scarred and bleeding; it rams first and keeps ramming, prioritizing the largest object in reach until something bigger makes it stop.
`encounter: 1: Kembingur Illhveli` | | 5 | **Plesiosaur Pack-Hunt (CR ~10)**. A trio rises from the shallows like spears, coordinating to flank and drag targets away from the ship into open water to finish the kill.
`encounter: 3: Plesiosaurus` | | 6 | **Kythri Chimera-Shallows (CR ~12)**. Wrong silhouettes ripple across the surface; the akhlut commits immediately while the leapers punish anyone who tries to reposition or break formation.
`encounter: 1: Akhlut, 3: Water Leaper` | | 7 | **Adder Bay Raiders (CR ~11)**. A disorganized rush surges from a kelp-choked trench; the bagiennik uses the chaos to net stragglers and anyone separated from the group.
`encounter: 4: Sea Spawn, 1: Bagiennik` | | 8 | **Shifting Glass Ambush (CR ~10)**. A glittering “safe channel” draws the eye; the bagiennik distracts, the glass gator hits from below, and the aalpamac collapses distance on anyone who tries to flee.
`encounter: 1: Bagiennik, 1: Glass Gator, 1: Aalpamac` | | 9 | **Froghemoth at the Kythri Swirl (CR 10)**. A rainbow-sheened vortex churns above a shattered reef, its colors folding like a living sky. The froghemoth is fully present nearby, nosing the seabed and snapping at drifting prey, repeatedly glancing toward the swirl as if expecting more to fall through.
Hostility triggers: approaching within 60 feet of the vortex, interacting with it (magic, probes, physical contact), or lingering for more than 2 rounds; once triggered, the froghemoth attacks with frantic urgency, attempting to grab and drag prey toward the reef beneath the swirling colors.
`encounter: 1: Froghemoth` | | 10 | **Isonade Storm-Lure (CR ~13)**. A tight squall blossoms overhead, lightning flickering in a spiral; the isonade rides the pressure change and watches.
Hostility Triggers: if the ship tries to outrun the storm, uses bright magic, or moves toward the calm eye; once engaged, it commits hard and controls the battlefield with weather.
`encounter: 1: Isonade` | ### Scenes and Situations ##### Situation 1 - [ ] - ##### Situation 2 - [ ] - ### Secrets and Clues Check off as information is received. These should be gathered from Secrets and Clues in Characters and Locations above, as well as anything particular to the Scenes and Situations in this adventure. - [ ] ### References -
